messages:
jordan: quick idea + question — thinking about doing a reshard of tenant queues into 'packing' vs 'isolation' lanes to reduce tail for small interactive requests. open to pushback. :thinking:

alina: love the intent. curious how you want to decide placement — size-based or priority hints?

jordan: main idea: use a cheap fast-path for requests < 64 tokens (packing lane) that aggressively coalesces into dense batches; large or high-throughput tenants go to isolation lanes. placement could be elastic: start in packing, spill on CPU/GPU contention.
sam: spill-on-contention sounds good but how do we avoid churn between lanes? moving a tenant back and forth could thrash.
jordan: right — propose a hysteresis window: require sustained congestion for 10s+ or X percent tail increase before moving. also track packing density metric so we don't move noisy tenants that occasionally send small requests.
maria: we need clear observable signals. suggest a quantile-aware headroom metric: 95th token-latency delta vs baseline. if delta > threshold and packing density < target -> move out.
alina: accounting question — do we keep a global credit pool for packing lane? token-bucket won't capture packing benefits well. credits that represent "pack slots" might work.
sam: can we make credits additive per tenant so they earn packing priority when they produce many small requests? prevents big tenants from hogging.
jordan: yep. credits accumulate at steady rate, consumed on enqueue into packing. eviction from packing consumes an extra penalty so repeat spillers cool down.
maria: edgecases: bursty tenants that are mostly small but occasionally need large batches. plan for a one-shot bypass API? e.g., request hint `force_isolation: true`.
jordan: exactly. add enqueue hint: { "target_lane": "packing|isolation|auto", "size_hint": 32 }. runtime ignores hints if impossible. keep API minimal.
alina: what about backpressure semantics between scheduler and runtime? should scheduler NACK or soft-degrade with longer tail?
sam: prefer soft-degrade for user-facing endpoints. NACK only for strict SLO tenants. NACK -> immediate client retry adds load. soft-degrade keeps request but de-prioritizes packing.
maria: we need rollout story: start with telemetry-only mode for a week, then opt-in on a few low-risk tenants, then canary across a pool. also we must expose a dashboard: packing_density, spill_rate, lane_moves, 95/99 latencies per lane.
jordan: rollout plan sounds good. I'll add a flag `scheduler.packing.experiment=true` and telemetry hooks.
alina: implementation detail: prefer per-worker fast-path so packing decisions don't require global consensus. keep global controller for rebalancing only.
sam: watch out for headroom mis-estimates if workers have skewed workloads. controller should periodically recompute global packing thresholds.
jordan: agreed. we'll keep local admission for low-latency decisions and periodic reconciliation every 30s.
maria: small note — make sure traces include lane decision and reason (density, contention, manual) for debugging.
jordan: adding to the RFC follow-up doc.
deploy-bot: canary config applied to cluster-3: scheduler.packing.experiment=true — monitoring enabled. :rocket:
maria: nice. let's monitor packing_density and 99.9 latency for interactive endpoints for the next 24h and reconvene.
jordan: thanks all — I'll push a lightweight PR with config, metric names, and the enqueue hint shape.
alina: ping me for review, I can help with the rate/credit math.
sam: I'll prototype the local admission codepath tomorrow.
maria: meeting in 24h to review telemetry — put notes in the RFC thread.
